facts.fact: MINEDH's Plano Tecnológico da Educação of May 2019, with targets for 2020-2025, sets a programme to create the SEGI academic information system, expand it to all secondary and primary schools with connectivity and develop or adapt an academic record platform for general education; its first-phase target is 100% of secondary and 10% of primary schools taking part, and the programme is costed at 39.36 million meticais a year.
facts.system: Sistema Electrónico de Gestão de Informação Académica (SEGI)

facts.fact: The plan of May 2019 names MINEDH as responsible for designing the SEGI programme, with provincial directorates, district services and schools implementing it, and its ICT department (DTIC) coordinating the plan; partners named are INAGE, MoRENet, two universities, the private sector and international organisations.

systems.system: Computer rooms, equipment and internet for schools
systems.country_label: salas de informática; conexão das escolas à Internet
systems.tiers: targets: computer rooms in 50% of secondary schools (350 rooms), internet in 80% of secondary and 20% of primary schools; primary schools encouraged to buy computers with local means and the ADE school grant

note: A plan, not a report of use: it gives no count of schools on SEGI in 2019, and says ICT in primary schools serves school management with very limited internet. SEGI is classed emis on its stated purpose (academic information management at the school, with an academic record platform to be built); the plan does not say in so many words that schools enter a record per learner, so the parent may prefer it unclassified. Finance is proposed only (1% of the goods and services budget, part of FASE, the ADE grant), not a budget line.
